rule: round 5 held-out labels: a session that changes the skill, converter or runtime must not read this file, LABELS-HELD5.md or the templates until release point 5 has scored them (EXCLUSIONS.md)
by: the round-5 held-out session, from each template's JSON (name, description, nodes, parameters, connections) and PLAN.md decisions (Phase 1 'Decisions taken here', Out of scope for v1), before running the analyzer on these templates
selection: splits.json heldOutFresh5 (round 5): every fresh held-out template, all eligible by the round-4 rule with amendment 1 (so outcome subscription by the analyzer) by construction
convention: as labels-held4.json: outcome under the PLAN's default for each question the file cannot settle; questions = kinds whose answer can change the outcome; mayAsk = fine to ask, outcome unchanged; uncertain = where a convention, not the file, decides the label
priorExposure: No analyzer outcome, target or eligibility reason for these 20 was on screen before labelling; their corpus.json entries were not opened (the walk and the draw printed counts only, the tests assert eligibility without printing). splits.json heldOutFresh5 shows every template's wake-up kind, and the redraw's stratum (manual) was known. Checking lint collisions printed the pools of seven undrawn walk entries; marking 2562 printed only the clause of its own hand call. The question kinds, target rules and surfaces come from reading analyze.mjs's source and capabilities.json (which kinds exist, when each is asked, which requirement each surface lacks), not from any output for these templates. 3200, 683 and 4036 (redrawn in for 1948, 4414 and 3259 by the blind fixture session) were labelled the same way: each redraw printed only the new id and stratum, and their corpus.json entries and any analyzer output for them were not opened before the label was written

labels.why: Form Trigger (no sign-in, a textarea of channel ids; responds after the last node) and a daily schedule at midnight (workflow timezone America/Vancouver) → default channel ids → split → RSS Read per channel feed URL built in a Set (URL from data) → Code labels videos of the last 3 days → filter → Set with a placeholder Google API key → Code builds the YouTube Data API URL → HTTP GET (URL from data) → merge → Telegram sendPhoto (chat id from $env), and two Basic LLM Chains (OpenAI, model steps) writing HTML → two Gmail sends to a fixed address. Telegram's key cannot run in an artifact: the artifact form hands each submission to a task. With no sign-in, who fills it in decides; the form is the most demanding wake-up beside the schedule
labels.uncertain: the form waits for the last node (responseMode lastNode), which a task hand-off cannot answer; the Telegram chat id is $env.TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID, which n8n refuses when env access is blocked in nodes (an instance setting, not the file); the manual branch is disabled
labels.ifAnswered: outsiders fill it in → hosted (key: model steps on the path), since the form waits for the run

labels.why: Form Trigger (no sign-in: a PDF CV, location, job type, salary, email; pinned data) → Extract From File (PDF) → Set → agent (Gemini 2.5 Pro, a model step) with the SerpAPI tool (a stored key) → Code parses JSON → Code builds HTML → Gmail send to the address from the form. SerpAPI's key cannot run in an artifact: a task picks each submission up. With no sign-in, who fills it in decides
labels.uncertain: a job hunter that asks for the submitter's email reads as a service for other people, so outsiders may well fill it in
labels.ifAnswered: outsiders fill it in → a cloud task behind a relay (the form does not wait for the run)

labels.why: Manual → Set (prompt, aspect, duration, Airtable base and table ids, a callback URL) → Code picks a random camera motion → HTTP POST to Luma's generations API with a stored header credential → Execution Data (no fields) → Airtable create in the base and table the Set names, with a stored Airtable token. Stored credentials, run on request: skill
labels.uncertain: the camera motion is Math.random(), so the prompt sent differs per run; the callback URL is placeholder text that is only sent as data, never called; Part 1 of a pair, the callback receiver is another workflow

labels.why: Manual trigger and an Execute Workflow Trigger (inputs facts and text; no caller in this file), both into the same chain: Code splits the text into sentences → split → Basic LLM Chain per claim with an Ollama chat model (bespoke-minicheck) → merge → filter on 'No' → aggregate → Basic LLM Chain summary (Ollama completion model). Model steps only, no secret or outside I/O; the sub-workflow trigger is the deciding wake-up, run on request like manual. A model needs sample access in an artifact, so a skill
labels.uncertain: the Ollama models are specialised local models; a Claude model answering the Yes/No check behaves differently, and the filter matches the exact string 'No'
labels.ifAnswered: none; with no model step this would be an artifact

labels.why: Every minute: Sheets read of the server list → HTTP GET http://{server} (host from data) → success output: Sheets append 'Alive'; error output: Gmail send (no recipient, a P91 placeholder) → Sheets append 'Down'. More often than hourly but not under a minute: a local task
labels.uncertain: down servers are found through the HTTP node's error output; the Gmail node has no recipient

labels.why: Manual → Sheets read of keywords → Split In Batches (6) → Wait → agent (OpenAI, a model step) with a structured output parser → Sheets update of the same tab matched on Number → back to the batches. A Sheets credential: skill

Manual → Set (PiAPI key left empty, theme, style) → HTTP POST to api.piapi.ai chat completions (a reseller, not OpenAI's host) → Code builds the image prompt → POST Midjourney task → Wait → GET task status (fixed host) → IF loop back to Wait → Switch → Set image URLs → POST Canvas (switchboard) design. Keys travel in headers from data; the POSTs are assumed writes until answered. Outside HTTP: skill
labels.uncertain: if piapi.ai's chat-completions path counts as a known LLM API, that call is a model step with a Claude substitution, not a write

labels.why: Every 15 minutes: Set a list of three URLs → split → HTTP GET each (URL from data). More often than hourly: a local task. The terminal GET's output is what compares

Google Sheets Trigger (row added, every minute; document and sheet ids left empty for the person) → HTTP POST to Dumpling AI scrape (header-auth credential; assumed a write) → HTML extract of the book list → split → HTML extract of title and price → sort by price → Convert to CSV → Gmail send with the CSV attached (recipient empty, a P91 placeholder). Polling every minute: a local task
labels.uncertain: the scrape body sends $('Trigger…') itself (the node proxy, not the row's URL field) as the url

labels.why: Manual → Set (Instagram account id, post_type http_reel, media URLs, caption) → Switch on post_type → container-create POSTs to graph.facebook.com (HTTP with a header credential) or the Facebook Graph API node → Set container id → Wait → status GET (query credential) → IF FINISHED → publish via HTTP or the Graph API node, else Wait loop. Stored Facebook credentials: skill. Despite the name, nothing schedules it

Manual → Set (domain, crawl limit, branding) → DataForSEO task POST (basic auth) → status GET with a 1-minute Wait loop → pages POST → Code extracts URLs → per batch of 100: Search Console searchAnalytics POST (Google OAuth, URL built from fixed hosts in an expression) → Wait → Set; then links POSTs for 404/301 pages → Code builds the report → Code renders HTML → Convert to File. Stored credentials: skill

labels.why: Google Drive Trigger (file created in a fixed folder; no poll times, so n8n's default every minute) → Send Email over SMTP to a fixed address. SMTP becomes the mail connector (a substitution to approve). Polling every minute: a local task

Three Cron triggers, each to its own Discord v1 webhook post with fixed text and an image link: weekly at 9 on two weekdays, and every 30 minutes. The webhook URL carries its token inline (a secret to store). The 30-minute schedule is more often than hourly but not under a minute: a local task
labels.uncertain: three independent schedules in one workflow; the weekday numbers and the texts disagree (Wednesday text on weekday 6), and the 30-minute 'good night' post reads like a test left on

labels.why: Daily at 08:00 (no workflow timezone) → Sheets read of past reviews, and a Code list of three competitors → ScrapingBee GET (API key inline, a placeholder) per competitor → HTML extracts → Item Lists split → Markdown → Merge keeping new reviews (by review URL) → Sheets append and Slack send to a channel by name. Daily fits a cloud task; the time of day needs the timezone
labels.uncertain: both Sheets nodes carry no credential
